Definition: from G1722 and G911; to whelm on, i.e. wet (a part of the person, etc.) by contact with a fluid:--dip.
BiblicalUsage: embáptō is a plain word for dip. In Matthew 26:23, the text says "He that dippeth [his] hand with me in the dish."
TheologicalSignificance: I take embáptō as it stands: dip.
